findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the core precheck establishes GENUINE bot-alert provenance (not a spoofable free-text `detected_by`): e.g. an allow-listed lane set combined with a corroborating unforgeable signal (alert-marker comment/tag written by the lane, or the alert ticket's create-event provenance), and add a negative test where ordinary work FORGES a supported `detected_by` value and is still refused.
evidence: Design: 'may bypass completion verification only for tickets carrying bot-alert provenance (detected_by / bridge-alert metadata from the alert lane). A normal task/bug without that provenance must still be refused.'
src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:310 resolve_detected_by returns the explicit param or the REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — arbitrary free-text, no allow-list or unforgeable marker
scripts/canary_bridge.py:449 and scripts/dependency_audit.py:547 set --detected-by to plain strings ('heartbeat-canary', 'dependency-advisory-canary') that any caller can replicate

findings.finding: The provenance gate keys on `detected_by`, which is arbitrary caller-supplied free-text (explicit `--detected-by` or `REBAR_DETECTED_BY` env), so any ordinary work close can spoof a supported lane value and obtain the verifier bypass — the route becomes a general-purpose gate bypass, contradicting the plan's stated goal of narrowing it to bot-alert provenance.

REBAR_DETECTED_BY is set in a CI env, silently stamping supported provenance on unrelated closes

findings.finding: The plan pins the negative core path (non-bot-alert ticket refused) but never pins the positive core path: that a ticket carrying real bot-alert provenance is actually ACCEPTED by the new close-precheck branch and bypasses the completion verifier. The three script argv tests assert only that the argv survives the real `rebar transition` parser — not that the core gate lets the close through for a provenanced ticket. A core bug that rejects env_integration closes for legitimately-provenanced bot-alert tickets (e.g. reading the wrong provenance field, or requiring metadata the lanes do not actually stamp) would pass all six ACs while leaving all three lanes unable to close the tickets they filed — the exact 'latent failure for a certain one' outcome the plan's own 'Why it was not fixed there' section warns against.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 6 / Acceptance criteria (core test only proves the refusal)
scenarios: Core precheck reads provenance from the wrong snapshot field; genuine bot-alert tickets are refused; all three lanes silently fail to close on clear, yet argv tests + negative test are green
The alert lanes stamp provenance under a key the core gate does not recognize; the accept path is never exercised by any test

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name whether the alert tickets are type `bug` or non-bug, and state whether `close_class_refusal`/`ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES` (`txn.py:244`) must also be amended so `--class env_integration` is accepted on the (non-bug) alert tickets — otherwise the completion-gate-only bypass in step 2 will not let the close through.
evidence: txn.py:244: `elif close_class and close_class not in close_disposition.ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES:` -> refusal 'closing a {ticket_type} accepts --class only for an administrative disposition'
close_disposition.py:53: `ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES = frozenset({"duplicate", "obsolete", "superseded", "wontfix"})` — env_integration is absent
Current scripts pass `--class env_integration` together with `--force=<reason>` (dependency_audit.py:567-582); the plan removes `--force` but does not address close_class_refusal
Plan step 2 only mentions 'skips the completion verifier'; it never names close_class_refusal / ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES
findings.finding: The plan asserts bot-alert tickets can be closed with `--class env_integration` and no `--force`, but a gate-independent write-side guard (`close_class_refusal` in `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:212-251`) refuses `--class env_integration` on any NON-BUG close because `env_integration` is not in `ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES` (`src/rebar/_commands/close_disposition.py:53`). This guard is not the completion-verification gate the plan's step 2 targets; its docstring states 'neither --force nor a disabled completion gate skips it.' The plan's mechanism as described is therefore not achievable without also amending this guard (or establishing that the alert tickets are type `bug`), which the plan does not name.
scenarios: A bot-alert ticket that is NOT a bug type reaches close_class_refusal and is rejected before the completion verifier runs, so the clear-condition close fails at runtime on all three lanes after --force is removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend step 2 to cover the gate-independent write-side class guard: either establish that bot-alert tickets are `bug` type (which admits the full vocabulary including env_integration), or scope a provenance-gated exception in `close_class_refusal` so a bot-alert non-bug ticket may carry `--class env_integration`, and add the corresponding positive core test that the close is ACCEPTED end-to-end (not merely that the completion verifier is skipped).
